title: Instruction at Clark and classmates who became musicians
summary: The band director helped slower students; of 65 in the band only David Grillier and Batiste remained professional.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Now, did you get a lot of, when you were in Clark, did you get a lot of hands-on instruction? Yeah.

The man was very tentative to each one of his kids, especially the slow kids. The slow kids, he attended to, gave us some attention and tutoring personally. The faster kids would help the slower kids. Uh-huh.
Yeah. Were you one of the faster?
No. I was in between. Uh-huh.
I was in between. So who out of that Clark band went on to, that we would know, that went on to be a musician?
Well, out of our band, oh boy.
Those who dropped out, and there are a lot of them who died, some of them who died. And out of- .

The 65, there's two of us. David Grillier is a clarinet saxophone player, and he also now plays with Preservation Hall as one of the main characters. And myself are the only ones left out of our Clark High School in music. Out of 65. There are 17 who I know I did.
They didn't play. A lot of them didn't get to be professional. Eugene Jones was a drummer who played with Frogman. Okay, he was our bass drummer. He's deceased.

Yeah, yeah. John Walters, that was Piggy's son. I mean, Piggy, his name was Piggy. John Walters Sr. was his father. So that's one, two, that played professionally I would say. They got a lot of them that went into professional businesses and professional things and teaching and so forth, but they never played anymore. Like Wesley McJulian was in our class. He was an alto player. He's Dr. Wesley McJulian. He wasn't very much seventh grade now. I'm not even mentioning the other people because they died. Some of them didn't get into professional music before they died. There's youngsters coming up after we left high school. I say youngsters, but they just gave up music. But professionally, David Grillo and myself, we're the only ones right now.
